title: Arete 27B Pricing 2026: Plans, Limits and Alternatives
summary: Arete 27B pricing offers multiple tiers with different monthly costs and usage limits. Compare your options to pick the right plan.
body_markdown:
## Capping Arete 27B spend with Activepieces


Because the quote is only as good as the volume behind it,[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/blog/arete-27b-by-nous-research-what-we-know-2026) sets per-project and per-person AI caps and shows usage by team, so spend on a model is bounded and visible before the invoice.


Activepieces runs whichever model you already chose, on your own provider key, so Arete 27B's metered usage bills to your account at your rate.


Bring-your-own-key starts on the Plus plan at $20 a month, where every AI step counts as 1 credit whatever the model, against 2, 10 or 20 credits for a fast, smart or frontier model when a platform supplies the model itself.


A platform that resells you its own model has made that choice and priced it before you open the product, which is why the workflow below governs your usage and leaves Arete's rates alone.


### Where it genuinely helps


This matters only if you call the API.


In[Tran's REALM 2026 analysis of agent workflows](https://aclanthology.org/2026.realm-1.24.pdf) , the recurring prefix (instructions and history re-sent on every call) is **76.6% of billed input tokens** .


Three-quarters of your input bill is text you already paid for, so the number to watch is calls per day, not words per prompt.


Trim your own prompts and you attack the smallest slices: tool results are 16.9%, and echoed output is 6.5%. Read that split as a case for capping call count first, since every extra run re-buys the prefix. I'm ready to receive the sentences with numbers that need their consequences explained. Your message appears incomplete, it ends at "1." without the sentences themselves. Please provide the full list of sentences you'd like me to complete. Count today's runs at the start of each trigger. 2. Stop at the daily cap, so a looping agent hits a wall instead of your invoice. 3. Call the model with a limited retry, because each retry re-sends the full prefix at full price. 4. Log tokens used to a row, one per run, so you can bill each client for what their runs consumed. 5. Route simple tasks to the cheaper model, reserving Arete 27B for work that needs it.


Of the five, step 4 is the one an agency should care about most.


### What it cannot change


No workflow can lower Arete's per-token price, raise its rate limits or alter what the maker meters separately. If the quote you collected looks wrong, the fix is a different plan or a different vendor, not a cleverer automation.


> Without per-run rows, a shared account quietly makes light clients subsidize heavy ones.


The cap also protects only the calls routed through it; anything hitting the API directly bypasses your counter.


If you only use chat, you can skip all of this. With no API calls, there's no prefix to re-send and nothing for a workflow to count.


Activepieces is the better fit for teams that already chose their model and call it through their own API, judged on who controls the AI decision and what it costs to keep that control.


Bring-your-own-key starts on the Plus plan at $20 a month, with every AI step counting as 1 credit whatever the model, whereas a platform that resells its own model charges 2, 10 or 20 credits depending on the model tier it picked for you.


Per-project and per-person caps with usage shown by team keep spend bounded, though this matters only if you call the API; a team that wants a platform to supply and manage the model has a different need.
